title: nd blend
parentNote: For the last week two letters have meant one sound — sh, ch, th. Today two letters mean two sounds, said so close together they feel like one: nd, as in sand. That is what a blend is, and it is worth saying out loud to your child, because the difference is the whole lesson. What usually goes wrong is the d falling off the end, so "sand" comes out "san" and "hand" comes out "han"; children hear the word fine, they just stop early. Stretch the n out yourself — sannnn-d — and land hard on the d, then say it at normal speed. Ask them to feel their tongue flick down off the roof of the mouth for that last little tap.

activities.mouthCue: Tongue up behind your teeth and hum for n, then flick it down for d. Two taps in the same spot.
activities.prompt: This pair is not like sh or ch. Here you really do hear both letters — they are just in a hurry.

Hold the n for a long time, then tap the d: sannnn-d.

activities.title: The tin in the sand
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Tom and Pam did dig in the sand.
Pam got a big tin with a lid on top.
The tin had sand in it!
Tom did grin and hid the tin in the sand.

questions.prompt: Tom and Pam did dig in it.
It did dig and got the big tin.
